## Overview of the Enriched Pathways

In Table 1, we rank the enriched biological pathways based on a combination of statistical significance, biological coherence, and relevance to Parkinson’s disease. A prominent theme is the convergence of extracellular matrix and adhesion biology, highlighted by extracellular matrix organization (REAC:R-HSA-1474244, p = 0.0030007013052328036), focal adhesion (KEGG:04510, p = 0.021270340507868357), cell-matrix adhesion (GO:0007160, p = 0.0033551375900958635), Integrin cell surface interactions (REAC:R-HSA-216083, p = 0.0006274793748841679), integrin binding (GO:0005178, p = 6.567673799645586 × 10−5), and protein complex involved in cell adhesion (GO:0098636, p = 4.227289989050737 × 10−7). These findings suggest that altered neuron-glia attachment, extracellular matrix remodeling, and integrin-dependent signaling may contribute to dopaminergic neuron vulnerability, impaired synaptic stability, and neuroinflammatory responses in Parkinson’s disease, which is consistent with literature linking matrix dysregulation and adhesion signaling to neurodegeneration.

A second major signal involves innate immunity and phagocytic function, including opsonin binding (GO:0001846, p = 8.045019491307402 × 10−5), phagocytosis (GO:0006909, p = 0.01577821490041697), Phagosome (KEGG:04145, p = 0.00211427835887164), and TYROBP causal network in microglia (WP:WP3945, p = 0.002334528204237097). These pathways support a role for activated microglia and altered clearance of cellular debris, protein aggregates, and damaged synaptic material in Parkinson’s disease. This interpretation agrees with a large body of literature showing that microglial activation, complement-associated engulfment, and phagolysosomal dysfunction are central features of Parkinson’s disease progression. The enrichment of external side of plasma membrane (GO:0009897, p = 1.8623618097060346 × 10−6; associated proteins counts = 7) further supports the involvement of cell-surface immune and adhesion molecules in these processes.

In addition, Hippo Merlin signaling dysregulation (WP:WP4541, p = 0.0015619364291174415) points to altered stress-response and survival signaling, which may influence neuronal maintenance and degeneration. The tissue-enrichment signals for pituitary gland (HPA:0370000, p = 0.005159898078738623) and adrenal gland medullary cells (HPA:0020061, p = 0.002565623014107578) may reflect neuroendocrine and catecholamine-related aspects of Parkinson’s disease biology, consistent with evidence that systemic stress pathways and autonomic dysfunction accompany disease progression. Overall, the strongest pattern in these results is the intersection of extracellular matrix remodeling, integrin-mediated adhesion, microglial phagocytosis, and cell-surface immune signaling, suggesting that Parkinson’s disease is shaped not only by intrinsic neuronal injury but also by altered neuron-microenvironment interactions and chronic inflammatory clearance mechanisms.
